channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Uzbekistan Central Bank forecasts inflation to reach 5% by 2027
item.description: Uzbekistan's Central Bank projects inflation to decrease to 5% by 2027. The bank anticipates achieving its target inflation rate next year. These forecasts update previous projections regarding price increases in the country.

item.title: Nora Jeruto wins silver for Kazakhstan in Asian Games steeplechase
item.description: Former Kenyan athlete Nora Jeruto secured a silver medal for Kazakhstan in the women's 3000m steeplechase at the 2026 Asian Games. She finished second with a season-best time of 9:06.82, behind Bahrain's Winfred Yavi who set a new Games record.

item.title: Thirteen individuals sentenced in Almaty for altering vehicle identification numbers
item.description: A criminal group of 13 people in Almaty has been convicted for illegally registering vehicles and altering their VIN codes and electronic data. The group sold the cars through fraudulent means. Court sentences ranged up to eight years imprisonment, according to the Ministry of Internal Affairs.

item.title: Uzbekistan Agency to Assist Family of Child Victim of Violence Relocate
item.description: Uzbekistan's National Social Protection Agency is providing comprehensive support to the family of a 5-year-old girl who was a victim of sexual violence in Uchqo'rg'on district. The agency will facilitate the family's relocation to another city, providing housing and rehabilitation. The mother will receive assistance with education and employment, and the child's surname can be changed if necessary.

item.title: Irtysh River in Kazakhstan to Receive Personal Digital Passport
item.description: Kazakhstan's East Kazakhstan region has proposed creating a unified digital passport for the Irtysh River. This initiative aims to consolidate data on water depth, quality, riverbanks, fish stocks, and navigation into an updated information system. The digital passport will aid regions in planning transportation, dredging, and port infrastructure, potentially involving collaboration with Russia.

item.title: Astana Mayor Reports 60% Employment Rate for Free Course Graduates
item.description: In Astana, 60% of graduates from the free JOLTAP courses have found employment, according to city mayor Zhenis Kassymbek. Over three years, 22,000 individuals have trained in fields like sewing, welding, and SMM. An additional 17% work as freelancers, and about 2,000 have started small businesses. The program is expanding nationwide.

item.title: Three Servicemen Awarded 'For Courage' Medals Following Caspian Tragedy
item.description: Three servicemen have been awarded the 'For Courage' medal in recognition of their bravery and selflessness during a training exercise that resulted in the deaths of 14 military personnel in the Caspian Sea. The Defense Minister was dismissed following the incident.

item.title: Old Video Circulating Online with False Context Regarding Caspian Tragedy
item.description: A video circulating on social media, falsely linked to the recent deaths of servicemen in Mangystau, has been debunked. Investigations revealed the video was first posted in August 2026 and shows a vehicle registered in the Turkestan region, predating the September incident.

item.title: Karaganda region deploys 19 checkpoints to combat cattle theft
item.description: Karaganda region has established 19 mobile checkpoints on roads to prevent cattle and meat product theft. The measure, active until winter, involves checking transport and documentation for origin and legality. Police reported 25 cattle theft cases this year, with 14 solved.

item.title: Trump Rejects Iran's Ceasefire Proposal, Citing Unsatisfactory Terms
item.description: US President Donald Trump rejected Iran's proposal for a ceasefire, stating the terms were unacceptable. Iran had offered to open the Strait of Hormuz to commercial vessels and resume nuclear talks if sanctions were lifted and a ceasefire held in Iran and Lebanon.

item.title: Tajik President Emomali Rahmon offers condolences to Kazakhstan over military deaths
item.description: Tajik President Emomali Rahmon has expressed his condolences to Kazakhstan's President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev following the deaths of 14 Kazakh soldiers during a military exercise. The exact circumstances of the incident were not detailed in the report.

item.title: Germany identifies 488 Afghans for potential deportation, including 267 without criminal records
item.description: German authorities have identified 488 Afghan nationals for possible deportation, with 267 having no criminal convictions, according to the Interior Ministry. Since the current government took office, around 250 Afghan nationals have been deported. Deportations to Afghanistan resumed in 2024.

item.title: Video Linked to Caspian Tragedy Filmed in Morocco, Not Kazakhstan
item.description: A video circulating on social media, purportedly showing a mother grieving a soldier lost in the Caspian Sea tragedy, was filmed in Tangier, Morocco. The video's author confirmed it has no connection to Kazakhstan.

item.title: Iran's Revolutionary Guard Threatens to Attack US Ships in Indian Ocean
item.description: Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) has threatened to attack US ships in the Indian Ocean if a new war breaks out. Deputy political commander Ali Mohammadi stated Iran would "undoubtedly attack and destroy" US vessels. Tensions remain high between the US and Iran over the Strait of Hormuz.

item.title: Kazakhstan Disinformation Center Addresses Fake News on Mangystau Tragedy
item.description: Kazakhstan's Center for Combating Disinformation has highlighted fake news surrounding the Mangystau tragedy, where 14 servicemen died. Despite official updates, social media users spread unverified information, archive videos, and AI content. The center noted coordinated efforts from anonymous accounts to spread rumors.

item.title: Donald Trump rejects Iran's offer to reopen Strait of Hormuz
item.description: U.S. President Donald Trump has rejected Iran's proposal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz. Iran had offered to reopen the strait within seven days if a deal was reached with the U.S., which included lifting sanctions and unblocking Iranian assets. The Wall Street Journal reported that Trump might restart military strikes against Iran after the U.S. midterm elections in November.

item.title: Clash in Nuristan; Taliban report 28 killed and 32 detained
item.description: A clash occurred in Nuristan, with the Taliban reporting 28 individuals killed and 32 others detained. Further details about the incident were not provided.

item.title: Tragedy on Caspian Sea: Kazakhstan President appoints new Defense Minister
item.description: Kazakhstan's President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev appointed Aidoss Myrzakhmetov as the new Defense Minister following a tragedy during military exercises. Five officers are detained in connection with the incident where 12 servicemen died and two are missing.

item.title: Kazakh Police Punish Perpetrators of Fake News About Caspian Military Tragedy
item.description: Kazakhstan's Center for Combating Disinformation reported that police have apprehended individuals spreading false information about a recent military tragedy in the Caspian Sea. The center refuted claims of hidden death tolls, incorrect deployment methods, and a drunk commander, clarifying that 14 servicemen died and their identities were released.

item.title: Kazakhstan Courts Receive 45 Criminal Cases Against Organized Crime Group Members This Year
item.description: Kazakhstan's Ministry of Internal Affairs reported that 45 criminal cases against members of organized crime groups have been sent to courts this year. Recent convictions include sentences up to 13 years for theft from mining enterprises and up to 10 years for similar property theft. In Almaty, 13 individuals were sentenced up to eight years for illegal vehicle registration and fraud.

item.title: Almaty Marathon Boosts City Economy Through Tourism and Spending
item.description: The Almaty Marathon significantly impacts the city's economy, attracting participants from abroad and other regions of Kazakhstan. These visitors, along with their companions, contribute substantially to the hospitality, transport, retail, and entertainment sectors. In 2026, the economic contribution of running events is projected to reach 15.6 billion tenge, with significant tax revenues.

item.title: Taliban Distributes Over 827,000 Electronic National ID Cards in Six Months
item.description: The Taliban announced the distribution of 827,060 electronic national identity cards, or e-Tazkiras, nationwide within the first six months of the current year. Of these, 600,546 were issued to men and 226,524 to women. Kabul saw the highest distribution with 232,996 cards.

item.title: Expert: New Defense Minister's Appointment Reflects Meritocracy Principles
item.description: Political scientist Adil Seifullin commented on the appointment of the new Defense Minister, linking it to a practice of appointing officers from the State Security Service to leadership roles in complex state sectors. He noted that officers who served in the State Security Service have proven their competence, citing improvements in the National Security Committee and the Ministry of Emergency Situations.

item.title: OCHA Reports Severe Restrictions on Humanitarian Access in Four Afghan Districts
item.description: The UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA) reports severe restrictions on humanitarian activities and access to aid recipients in four Afghan districts. OCHA cited administrative interference, restrictions on female aid workers and recipients, project delays, movement restrictions, and funding cuts as key factors limiting access.

item.title: Kazakhstan President Awards State Honors to Military Personnel Lost in Caspian Sea Exercises
item.description: Kazakh President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev has awarded state honors for courage to military personnel who died during exercises in the Caspian Sea. The Akorda reported that survivors were also recognized with state awards.

item.title: Kazakh President Orders New Defense Minister to Prioritize Servicemember Safety
item.description: President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev has instructed the new Minister of Defense to make the safety of military personnel an absolute priority. The directive was issued following recent events.

item.title: Taliban Ministry of Justice Seizes Nearly 300 Acres of Land in Balkh Province
item.description: The Taliban's Ministry of Justice announced the seizure of approximately 297 acres of land in Balkh province, Afghanistan. The ministry stated the land belonged to the "Khatam al-Anbia Project" and was located in Mazar-e-Sharif. Documents were reviewed by a special court.

item.title: Kazakhstan Warns of Legal Action for Spreading False Information on Military Incident
item.description: Kazakhstan's Center for Combating False Information reported that social media users are spreading unverified claims and unrelated videos regarding the deaths of military personnel in Mangystau. The center clarified that the actual number of deceased was 14 and debunked claims about helicopter deployment and the origin of circulated videos.

item.title: Nineteen Checkpoints Established in Karaganda Region to Combat Cattle Rustling
item.description: Nineteen mobile checkpoints have been set up on roads in the Karaganda region to combat cattle rustling, a common issue during the autumn livestock slaughter season. Police are inspecting vehicles transporting livestock and meat, verifying origin documents. Last year, these checkpoints helped uncover eight cases of cattle theft.

item.title: Russia Updates Depression Treatment Standards with New Procedures
item.description: Russia's updated health standards will allow more procedures for recurrent depression patients, including electro-acupuncture and laser blood irradiation. The new regulations, effective October 3, replace 2022 guidelines and also include enhanced patient screening and psychiatric observation.

item.title: Family of Sexual Assault Victim to Relocate with Support from National Agency
item.description: The family of a girl who was a victim of sexual assault in Namangan will relocate to another city. Shahnoza Mirziyoyeva, deputy director of the National Agency for Social Protection, stated that all necessary conditions will be created for the child and her relatives to start a new life in a safe place.

item.title: Taliban and Pakistani Forces Exchange Fire for Two Hours on Border
item.description: Sources in Paktia province report a two-hour clash between Taliban fighters and Pakistani soldiers along the Durand Line late Saturday. Both sides used light and heavy weapons, but no casualties have been reported. Tensions remain high due to recent Pakistani airstrikes on Afghan territory.

item.title: US Experts Express Concern Over Saudi Arabia's Nuclear Ambitions
item.description: US experts have voiced concerns that Saudi Arabia has not abandoned its pursuit of nuclear weapons. They worry that the US may assist Saudi Arabia in developing its nuclear program, potentially intensifying an arms race in the Middle East. The report cites a US analyst's assessment.

item.title: Kazakh President Honors Soldiers Lost in Caspian Sea Exercise Tragedy
item.description: Kazakh President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev signed a decree posthumously awarding state honors to soldiers who died during exercises in the Caspian Sea. The incident on September 24th resulted in 12 deaths, with two still missing. The soldiers were participating in drills near Aktau.

item.title: Tajikistan begins autumn conscription campaign for military service
item.description: Tajikistan's autumn conscription campaign for military service commenced on October 1 and will continue until November 30. Key questions regarding the draft process have been answered.

item.title: Taliban declare 600 jeribs of land in Balkh 'state property'
item.description: The Taliban's Ministry of Justice announced that a special court has designated 600 jeribs of land in Balkh province, known as the "Khatam-al-Anbiya Project," as state property. This follows a similar declaration for land in Mazar-i-Sharif.

item.title: Taliban Reports Over 100 Migrant Families Returned to Afghanistan
item.description: The Taliban's spokesperson announced that 135 migrant families, totaling 613 individuals, returned to Afghanistan. Families entered through various crossings including Torkham, Spin Boldak, Silk Bridge, and Islam Qala, according to the statement.

item.title: Kazakh President Dismisses Defense Minister After Caspian Sea Tragedy
item.description: Kazakh President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev has dismissed Defense Minister Dauren Kosanov following the deaths of 14 servicemen during naval exercises in the Caspian Sea. The ministry cited sudden severe weather as the cause. A commission will investigate the defense ministry's affairs.

item.title: Tokayev Sacks Defense Minister After Caspian Military Incident
item.description: Kazakh President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev dismissed Defense Minister Dauren Kosanov on September 27 following the deaths of 14 servicemen during naval exercises in the Caspian Sea. A new minister, Aydos Sakenovich Mirzakhmetov, has been appointed. Criminal cases have been initiated.

item.title: Over 60 individuals defrauded in Bukhara using malicious APK files
item.description: Authorities in Bukhara have arrested individuals suspected of stealing money from over 60 people using malicious APK files. The criminal scheme was reportedly orchestrated by a young individual under 20 from the Samarkand region and their accomplices in various areas.
